content: The dispute concerned a postal account and fruit-bearing bonds (buoni fruttiferi) cashed by the wife shortly before the finality of the separation. For assets falling into the comunione de residuo under Art. 177(c) CC, such as bank accounts, the claimant bears the burden of proving that savings actually existed at the specific moment the community was dissolved. Conversely, for the bonds, even if purchased with personal gift money, the act of jointly titling them in the names of both spouses unequivocally expresses an intent to include them in the community, thereby granting each spouse a right to 50% of the total value upon dissolution.
